newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firm Sahaviriya City fails on bond payments.
newsitem.headline: Thai firm Sahaviriya City fails on bond payments.

text.p: Major Thai property developer, Sahaviriya City Plc, said on Thursday it was negotiating with bond holders following defaults on interest payments and hoped that a settlement could be reached soon.

Cimi Tan, senior vice president of Sahaviriya City, told Reuters that the default on the interest payments on the bonds resulted from a postponement of the company's initial public offering last year whereby more funds could not be raised.

A spokeswoman of Bangkok's Bond Dealers Club told Reuters that Sahaviriya City defaulted on on its semiannual interest payment on 750 million baht worth of nonconvertible bonds on April 29. The two-year-old bond matures on April 29, 1998 and carries a 14.25 percent interest.
"The delay on the interest payments mainly resulted from our delay on the IPO in the Thai stock market from last year. I believe the company has no financial problems," said Cimi.
"Negotiations with bond holders are going very well. We have difficulties but we believe we can tackle them," Cimi said.

Sahaviriya City has a total registered capital of 2.1 billion baht ($80.77 million). Sahaviriya Group holds 60 percent out of the total stakes while the remainder is held by Hong Kong's New Way Group.

Thailand's property sector has been grappling with a major glut, double-digit interest rates and over-leveraged, inexperienced property and development companies which have been hit by cash flow problems.
But Cimi said his company had no problems on its condominium business.
"Sahaviriya City is lucky because its present (condominium) project is going to become an area of growth in terms of commercial and residential in future," Cimi said.
The project is completed and property has been put up for sale.
